record.question: G05 (DLC-114)
record.title: Best 2kWh portable power station for an RV under $900 (2026): what a 30-amp RV plug really gets
record.h1: Best 2kWh portable power station for an RV under $900 (2026)
record.desc: Which 2kWh portable power station to buy for an RV under $900: five LiFePO4 stations compared on the TT-30 (30-amp RV) outlet, output, solar input, weight and price on the makers' US stores, with what a 30-amp RV plug really gets from a 2,400 W inverter and the code that worked in BLUETTI's cart.
record.intro:
Short answer. Buy the BLUETTI AC200L ({buy:bluetti-ac200l}), under $900: it is a 2kWh portable power station with a built-in TT-30 (30-amp RV) outlet, so the RV's plug goes straight into it: 2,048 Wh LiFePO4, 2,400 W, 1,200 W of solar input. Three things to know before you plug in the RV. First, the RV plug gets about 20 A, not 30 A: the 2,400 W inverter runs the RV fridge, water pump, lights and a coffee maker, not the full 30 A service or the rooftop AC. Second, once plugged in, the RV's converter charges its house battery from the power station (up to about 800 W), so switch the converter off once that battery is full. Third, set a two-way fridge to propane: on AUTO it uses 2.4–3.6 kWh a day, more than the whole 2kWh pack.

The AC200L is late in its life (BLUETTI Canada lists it as discontinued) but was in stock on bluettipower.com on 2026-10-31. The other RV power stations with a TT-30 under $900 are Anker's SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 ($899.99, the lightest at 41.7 lb) and the Renogy PowerStation 2000 ($849).
record.after:
How long a 2kWh power station lasts in an RV

A 12 V compressor fridge uses about 0.7 kWh a day, a furnace blower 0.3–0.5 kWh on a cold night, and lights, phones and the water pump about 0.2 kWh: roughly 1.2–1.5 kWh a day. That is about a day and a half with no sun, and two to three days with 200–400 W of solar. A 13,500 BTU rooftop AC needs 2,800–3,500 W to start (about 2,000 W with a soft starter) and runs 1,300–1,900 W, so a 2kWh station runs it for about an hour.

Recharging on the road

  • Campground or home outlet: about 1–1.5 hours on a 15/20 A outlet.
  • Driving: a DC-DC alternator charger adds 560–800 W; the 12 V socket gives about 100 W, a full day for a full charge.
  • Solar: a 400 W panel returns about 1–1.5 kWh on a good day. The AC200L and Renogy take 1,200 W, the Elite 200 V2 1,000 W, Anker 800 W, Jackery 400 W.

The Elite 200 V2 is lighter and rated for twice the cycles of the AC200L, but has no RV outlet: it needs a 5-20P to TT-30R adapter and is then limited to that outlet's 20 A. Jackery's Explorer 2000 v2 is a popular pick but was $999 on Jackery's store on 2026-10-31 and has no RV outlet.
